source_evidence.location: Section 1.3, printed page 9, immediately after Theorem 1.3.2
source_evidence.observation: The printed sentence states that the CDF of the normalized sum converges pointwise to the CDF of the standard normal distribution.

binders: A sequence of random variables X1, X2, ...
The index N tending to infinity
hypotheses: X1, X2, ... are independent and identically distributed.
The common mean is μ and the common variance is σ².
ZN = (SN − E SN) / sqrt(Var(SN)) = (1 / (σ sqrt(N))) times the sum from i = 1 to N of (Xi − μ).
conclusions: As N tends to infinity, the CDF of ZN converges pointwise to the CDF of the standard normal distribution.
definitions_and_conventions: The limiting distribution is the standard normal distribution N(0, 1).
Convergence in distribution is explained here as pointwise convergence of the normalized-sum CDF to the standard-normal CDF.
implicit_context: The sentence inherits the sequence, normalization, and standard-normal limit from Theorem 1.3.2.
The convergence parameter is N tending to infinity.

details: The CDF of the normalized sum ZN.
The CDF of the standard normal distribution N(0, 1).
Pointwise convergence of CDFs as N tends to infinity.
The printed sentence does not state a continuity-point restriction.

undebatable_constraints: The normalized-sum sequence is ZN from Theorem 1.3.2.
The limit is the standard normal distribution N(0, 1).
The source explicitly describes the CDF convergence as pointwise.
The printed explanatory sentence contains no continuity-point qualifier.

ambiguities.issue: The printed sentence gives unrestricted pointwise CDF convergence rather than explicitly restricting convergence to continuity points of the limiting CDF.
ambiguities.evidence: The sentence says that the normalized-sum CDF converges pointwise to the standard normal CDF and includes no continuity-point clause.
ambiguities.impact: The source contract must preserve the unrestricted pointwise wording in this inherited standard-normal context and must not attribute an explicit continuity-point restriction to the printed sentence.

contract_plain_english: For the normalized sums ZN in Theorem 1.3.2, convergence in distribution to N(0, 1) means that, as N tends to infinity, their CDFs converge pointwise to the standard-normal CDF. The printed sentence states no continuity-point restriction.
